newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: TENNIS-TOP SEED KAFELNIKOV CRASHES OUT OF SWISS OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-TOP SEED KAFELNIKOV CRASHES OUT OF SWISS OPEN.

text.p: Former-champions Yevgeny Kafelnikov and Albert Costa made unexpected first round exits from the Swiss Open on Tuesday.

Top seed Kafelnikov, the 1996 French Open champion and winner of the Swiss title in 1995, was brushed aside 6-4 6-3 by 1992 Olympic champion Marc Rosset while number five Costa, last year's Swiss Open champion, fell to American Richey Reneberg 6-2 1-6 6-4.
Rosset, who has seen his world ranking slip to 26, delighted the hometown Swiss fans as he overpowered the fifth ranked Russian in just 59 minutes.

"I wasn't surprised by the way I played and I wasn't surprised by the way he (Rosset) played," said Kafelnikov, a fourth round loser to Nicolas Kiefer at Wimbledon. "I've played one month on grass and I just didn't feel that comfortable."
Cedric Pioline, who lost in the Wimbledon final to Pete Sampras on Sunday, also struggled to find his footing back on clay.
The Frenchman appeared unsure as he dropped the first set to compatriot Fabrice Santoro before battling back to take a narrow three set decision, 3-6 6-2 7-6 (9-7).

"The change was difficult but I must forget about what happened last week, this is a new tournament," said Pioline, the first Frenchman since 1946 to reach the Wimbledon final. "I'm a bit tired mentally but because I played well last week doesn't mean I don't need to play well to win this week."
In sharp contrast, third seeded Spaniard Sergi Bruguera, playing in his first event since losing the French Open final to Gustavo Kuerten, as usual, looked completely at home on the slow red clay.
The winner of back-to-back French titles in 1993 and 1994, Bruguera showed no signs of rust as he easily disposed of 1987 Wimbledon champion Pat Cash of Australia, 6-3 6-1.

Fourth seed Marcelo Rios of Chile, who enjoyed unexpected success at Wimbledon advancing to the fourth round before falling to Boris Becker, made a smooth transition from grass back to clay brushing aside Brazilian qualifier Jaime Oncins 6-4 6-2.
Second seed Alex Corretja of Spain, the winner of two tournaments this season in Estoril and Rome, beat the Czech Republic's Jiri Novak 6-3 7-5, setting up a second round clash against Pioline.
